research_question: What is the effect of high-dose calcium supplementation (≥1 g elemental calcium per day) during pregnancy, compared with placebo or no treatment, on the risk of preterm birth before 37 weeks' gestation?
treatment_label: High-dose calcium supplementation during pregnancy (≥1 g elemental calcium/day)
outcome_description: Preterm birth, defined as delivery before 37 completed weeks' gestation. Extracted as the number of women/pregnancies with a preterm birth event and the total number randomized in each arm, restricted to trials (or trial arms) administering a high dose of calcium (≥1 g/day). Only the dose-stratified high-dose comparison is eligible; non-dose-stratified pooled analyses and timing-stratified ("started to take calcium before/after X weeks") analyses of the same outcome are excluded as separate analyses. Trials reporting zero preterm birth events in both arms are treated as not estimable and excluded from pooling.
positive_direction: A positive effect size (RR below 1 on the raw scale, re-signed so positive favors treatment) means high-dose calcium supplementation REDUCED the risk of preterm birth before 37 weeks compared with placebo or no treatment.

inclusion_criteria: Studies of calcium supplementation given to pregnant women, compared with placebo, no supplementation, or a lower/no-calcium control condition
Reports any quantitative data on preterm birth, gestational age at delivery, or delivery before 37 weeks (event counts, proportions, risk/odds ratios, or means with variability)
Any trial or controlled comparative study design in any country, language, or publication year, including trials where calcium was co-administered with other supplements
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, commentaries, opinion pieces, protocols, or purely theoretical/modelling papers)
No comparison between a calcium-supplemented condition and a placebo / no-treatment / control condition (e.g. single-arm or purely observational descriptive studies with no control group)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no event counts, proportions, means with SDs, t/F statistics, or risk/odds ratios reported or derivable)

Completely unrelated to the research topic (not about calcium supplementation in pregnancy or not reporting a preterm birth / gestational-length outcome), or reporting only the non-dose-stratified or timing-stratified ('started to take calcium') version of this outcome rather than a high-dose (≥1 g/day) comparison
moderators_to_extract: Baseline dietary calcium intake / population calcium status (low vs adequate)
Baseline risk of pre-eclampsia (high-risk vs average-risk women)
Gestational age at initiation of supplementation
Control condition type (placebo vs no treatment)
Sample size category and country income level
effect_size_note: Pool as a Risk Ratio (RR) using each trial's reported number of preterm birth events and total number randomized per arm (intention-to-treat denominators where available). Restrict extraction to the high-dose (≥1 g/day elemental calcium) subgroup of the dose-stratified analysis; do not extract the overall non-dose-stratified estimate or the timing-stratified estimate for this outcome. Trials with zero events in BOTH arms are not estimable and are excluded from pooling; single-zero-arm trials may be handled with a standard continuity correction or Mantel-Haenszel pooling without correction. Use a random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird or REML) with heterogeneity quantified by tau², I², and Cochran's Q.
